
```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from matplotlib import pyplot as plt
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
```

Load data from the previous notebook
```{python}
waveforms = np.load("spike_waveforms.npy")
```

## Finding the correct number of features

Initialize `PCA` to extract `n_components`
```{python}
n_components = 10
pca = PCA(n_components=n_components)
```

Create arrays to store PCA features and explained variance
```{python}
n_spikes, n_channels = waveforms.shape[1], waveforms.shape[-1]
pca_features = np.zeros((n_spikes, n_components, n_channels))
var_explained = np.zeros((n_components, n_channels))
```

For each channel, apply PCA and extract features. PCA expects the data to be organized samples-by-features so we have to transpose the matrix first.
```{python}
for i_ch in range(n_channels):
    X = waveforms[:,:,i_ch].T
    pca_features[:,:,i_ch] = pca.fit_transform(X)
    var_explained[:,i_ch] = pca.explained_variance_ratio_
```


Plot the explained variance
```{python}
plt.plot(range(1, n_components+1), var_explained, marker="o")
plt.xlabel("Component Number")
plt.ylabel("Explained Variance Ratio")
plt.show()
```

## Extract and save features

Based on the plot, we can see that 3 components account for most (~80%) of the variance in the data. Now, we extract three components
```{python}
n_components = 3
pca = PCA(n_components=n_components)
n_spikes, n_channels = waveforms.shape[1], waveforms.shape[-1]
pca_features = np.zeros((n_spikes, n_components, n_channels))
for i_ch in range(n_channels):
    X = waveforms[:,:,i_ch].T
    pca_features[:,:,i_ch] = pca.fit_transform(X)
```

Save the pca features
```{python}
np.save("pca_features.npy", pca_features)
```

## Visualization

Plot the first PC for all combinations of channels
```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(2,3)
p = 0
labels = ['Ch1','Ch2','Ch3','Ch4']
for i in np.arange(0,4):
    for j in np.arange(i+1,4):
        axis = ax.flatten()[p]
        axis.plot(pca_features[:,0, i], pca_features[:,0, j],'.k', markersize=.7) 
        axis.set(xlabel=labels[i], ylabel=labels[j], xlim=(-1500,1500), ylim=(-1500, 1500), xticks=[], yticks=[])
        p = p+1
plt.show()
```
